headline: Low interaction risk overall: dbt-core can write to warehouses while godot_rl_agents is local-only, so prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict pathways are limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No documented shared communication channel exists between dbt-core and godot_rl_agents. dbt-core only calls a data warehouse API and godot_rl_agents has no io_surfaces or network egress, so there is no plausible default path for one agent’s outputs to be parsed as instructions by the other.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies dbt-core output into a prompt or config consumed by godot_rl_agents, injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep outputs in separate files and do not paste between tools.
Require manual review before any copied text is reused as instructions.
Use distinct workspaces for analytics and game-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted egress, while godot_rl_agents is documented as network-egress none and touches no data classes. The pair does not show a shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage is limited to unusual operator bridging rather than a default cross-agent flow.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local workspace containing warehouse extracts, leakage risk increases.
IF dbt-core is configured to export warehouse contents into files later read by godot_rl_agents, sensitive data can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Store warehouse extracts in a restricted directory.
Do not mount the same workspace into both agents.
Review dbt outputs before sharing them externally.
Disable any ad hoc export step that feeds the game agent.
Use separate OS accounts for each agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core has allowlisted network egress and warehouse API access, while godot_rl_agents shows no network egress and no write surfaces. With no overlapping mutable resource or shared write path documented, direct capability conflict is unlikely and any contention would require extra orchestration not shown here.
conditions: IF an orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same warehouse objects or files, conflicts can occur.
IF future configuration adds shared git or filesystem writes, contention risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate resource namespaces.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same warehouse tables.
Serialize any shared updates through one operator.
Document ownership of mutable resources.
requires-engineering: add locking or transactional coordination for shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can produce warehouse-facing outputs, but godot_rl_agents has no documented downstream action-taking authority and no evidence that it treats dbt output as authoritative. Without a verified handoff, the cascade is limited to manual misuse rather than an automatic error chain.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs are fed directly into godot_rl_agents without validation, bad facts can propagate.
IF an operator uses dbt-generated artifacts as authoritative inputs for downstream actions, cascading errors become more likely.
mitigations: Add a human verification step before reuse of dbt outputs.
Label generated artifacts as untrusted until checked.
Keep action-taking systems separate from analytics generation.
Use schema checks on any transferred data.
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between producer and consumer.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, which may carry residency or retention obligations, while godot_rl_agents touches no data classes and has no documented compliance-sensitive handling. Because only one agent is clearly in scope, the main risk is a mismatch if warehouse data is exported into the other agent’s environment.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated records and is exported into godot_rl_agents, compliance scope expands.
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the warehouse and any copied artifacts, mismatch risk appears.
mitigations: Avoid exporting regulated warehouse data into local files.
Apply the warehouse retention policy to any derived artifacts.
Keep deletion requests synchronized across copies.
Review data classification before sharing outputs.
requires-engineering: implement centralized retention and deletion controls.
